captions.linkedin:
Peter Lynch ran Magellan from 1977 to 1990. We turned his playbook into a screen you can run tonight.

The strategy: BUY GROWTH AT REASONABLE PRICE. PEG ratio under 1, understandable business, clean balance sheet, multi-year hold.

Here's the complete logic, no black box:

🔹 PEG RATIO FILTER. Price-to-earnings divided by growth rate. Under 1 means you're paying less than the growth justifies.
🔹 GROWTH QUALITY CHECK. Revenue growth has to corroborate earnings growth. Otherwise it's accounting.
🔹 BALANCE SHEET TEST. Debt-to-equity under 0.5 to 1.0. Healthy current ratio. Survives the next recession.
🔹 CATEGORY FRAMEWORK. Sort every name into fast grower, stalwart, cyclical, turnaround, or asset play. Each gets different position sizing.
🔹 CONVICTION HOLD. Let winners compound. Only trim when the story breaks, not when the price wobbles.

Peter Lynch's GARP philosophy, One Up on Wall Street (1989) and Beating the Street (1993). Educational use only.

Peter Lynch ran Fidelity Magellan from 1977 to 1990 using one core rule: pay a P/E that's justified by the growth rate.

That's GARP. Growth At Reasonable Price. And it's mechanical enough to screen tonight.

The complete logic:

🔹 PEG ratio under 1 as the entry filter.
🔹 Revenue growth has to corroborate earnings growth, otherwise it's accounting tricks.
🔹 Debt-to-equity under 0.5 to 1.0, healthy current ratio.
🔹 Sort each name into fast grower, stalwart, cyclical, turnaround, or asset play. Position size by category.
🔹 Let winners compound. Only trim when the underlying story breaks.

Source: Peter Lynch, One Up on Wall Street (1989) and Beating the Street (1993). Educational use only.
